proposed_rules.trigger: A pair of [2x1] nodes at the very bottom of main content: first a marketing tagline ("The best no-code platform for..."), second a pipe-separated link list, appearing identically-structured across pages just before the cookie overlay.
proposed_rules.decision: Model as a global site footer fragment; exclude from the page's own block inventory.
proposed_rules.rationale: Mirrors the already-confirmed knack-announcement-bar treatment for header chrome; identical structural pair recurs at page bottom across unrelated templates.

proposed_rules.trigger: An FAQ accordion's expanded answer ([region] node) appears as a page-root sibling instead of nested under its question row, overlapping the FAQ section's y-range.
proposed_rules.decision: Fold the promoted [region] back into the FAQ block as the answer cell for the nearest preceding unanswered question, rather than treating it as a separate section.
proposed_rules.rationale: Absolute/overlay positioning during capture separates FAQ answers from their DOM parent, splitting one logical accordion row across the tree.

provenance.evidence: C139 rc4 [region] @130,3375 overlapping rc2c5 FAQ range 2656-3445

proposed_rules.trigger: A repeating grid/card container ([NxM] tag) whose extracted preview text is raw CSS selector syntax rather than real card copy.
proposed_rules.decision: Still model the container as a repeating-cards block per the generic rule; do not exclude as noise. Flag for phase-2 targeted extraction since the preview text is unreliable.
proposed_rules.rationale: The text-preview extractor grabbed a leaked inline <style> node instead of the first real content node; the grid itself is legitimate content (case study cards).

notes: Standard health-landing template: hero, case-study card grid, CTA banners, FAQ accordion, global footer/cookie chrome. Two capture artifacts found (leaked CSS text, promoted FAQ answer).
